findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path can abort the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use .map_err(|e| IoError::Read { path: path.to_string(), source: e }) or equivalent typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input; combined with lossy as cast as u16
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row (non-numeric second field) aborts the program; values >65535 silently truncate to u16 range
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)? or parse u32 then checked_into with typed error; return ParseError for invalid rows

findings.problem: Lossy width cast: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values >65535
findings.failure_mode: a sensor reading of 70000 becomes 4464 without any error or warning, corrupting domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange)? or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec<String> created from split
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-element CSV lines cause a panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and .ok_or(ParseError::Malformed) or guard with parts.len() check

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embedded in data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O side effect in what should be a pure data transformation; breaks testability and functional core purity; pollutes stdout
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if logging is needed, pass a callback or return a side-effect-free result; keep I/O at the shell boundary

findings.problem: load_sensors mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic without mocking the filesystem; parsing errors are conflated with I/O errors; violates functional core / imperative shell split
findings.fix: split into (a) shell function that reads the file and passes content to (b) a pure parse_sensors(&str) -> Vec<Record> or -> Result<..., ParseError> core function

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name with no domain validation; value is u16 with no range invariant
findings.failure_mode: any string including empty or whitespace-only becomes a valid sensor name; no type-level constraint on valid records
findings.fix: introduce a SensorName newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/whitespace; consider whether u16 value needs domain bounds

findings.problem: No error type defined; function returns Vec<Record> with no error channel
findings.failure_mode: all failure modes (I/O error, malformed lines, invalid numbers, out-of-range values, empty input) are collapsed into panics with no way for callers to distinguish or handle them
findings.fix: define a typed error enum (e.g., enum SensorError { Io(IoError), Malformed, Invalid, OutOfRange, Empty }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError>

findings.problem: collects all split parts into Vec<String> before accessing only the first two
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; each line allocates a Vec plus N String allocations for all fields, even when only 2 are needed
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Malformed)? to get exactly two &str parts with zero intermediate allocations

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity hint on the result Vec; unbounded growth from file input
findings.failure_mode: a very large file can exhaust memory with no early bound; no allocation-failure handling
findings.fix: accept a max_records parameter; call values.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| SensorError::Allocation)? before the loop

findings.problem: Validation and parsing are interleaved with iteration; no parse-boundary smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: partial records are silently dropped (iterator map + collect has no error short-circuit on unwrap panic); malformed lines at any position abort with panic rather than returning the first error
findings.fix: use try_fold or an explicit loop with early return on typed error to fail-fast on the first malformed line

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to validate any performance characteristics of the sensor loading path
findings.failure_mode: performance claims (if any) are unsubstantiated; no baseline for allocation count, throughput, or profiler data
findings.fix: add a workload-specific benchmark measuring lines-per-second, allocation count (allocations/lines), and peak memory for expected input sizes

findings.problem: No test module or behavior tests in the crate
findings.failure_mode: no executable evidence that the parsing logic handles valid input, empty files, malformed lines, out-of-range values, or I/O errors correctly
findings.fix: add tests covering: valid CSV input, empty file, malformed line (no comma), non-numeric value, out-of-range value (65536), empty name, and I/O error scenarios

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the sensor loading path
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf) to validate allocation behavior
no allocation counting evidence (e.g., alloc_counter, Criterion alloc tracking)
no second-ring integration test evidence (file-based end-to-end)
no command-line command evidence (no cargo test/cargo bench output present)
residual_risk: The function is fundamentally unsafe: three separate panic points (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, unchecked indexing) make it unsuitable for any production use. No error taxonomy, no functional core/shell split, and no tests exist. This crate requires a complete rewrite to be Holzman-compliant: introduce typed domain errors, a pure parse core, a shell boundary for I/O, and comprehensive tests. Without any of these, the failure surface covers all untrusted file inputs.
